g.text: Tracked certificate has passed its expiration threshold
IPACertmongerExpirationCheck reports ERROR for this certificate: Request id '20250801000000' status
MONITORING expired on 2026-08-01 00:00:00 UTC. Per Red Hat KCS 7007191 and
freeipa.org/page/V4/CA_certificate_renewal, an ERROR/CRITICAL result here means the certificate is at or
past expiry and effectively already service-impacting.
✓ IPACertmongerExpirationCheck reported ERROR: Request id '20250801000000' status MONITORING expired
Services relying on this certificate (LDAPS, HTTPS/Apache, or CA/KRA agent TLS) will fail TLS
Confirm the current certmonger tracking state for this request before acting.
Not caused by the problem above - each needs its own investigation.
Elevated disk usage on a Directory Server-critical path (possibly transient)
usage, but this is a single snapshot with no journalctl evidence of an actual write/space failure yet.
This matches a common transient pattern (an in-progress backup, a temporary log burst, or a log-rotation
job) just as well as it matches chronic unbounded growth.
/var/lib/dirsrv/ is using more than 80% of the available space.

Low immediate impact today; if usage keeps growing unchecked this can escalate to write failures or a
